_metadata.independence: I read only u22-blind-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or API was consulted.

hints.reason: Heart racing is a familiar phrase, but nothing about a mouse races; wholly one-sided.
Timid as a mouse is proverbial; heart only via a timid or faint heart, a loose shared-property route.
Mickey Mouse is instant, but Mickey has no route to heart.

best_available.why: Only hint that touches both words; mouse is proverbial and a timid heart is at least readable.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; RACING and MICKEY are pure mouse-or-heart filler.

hints.reason: Date night is a set phrase; heart reached only through romance as the symbol of love.
Lonely hearts (club, column) and a lonely night are both everyday phrases.
Heartbeat is immediate; night has no beat route beyond a strained nightclub or police-beat reading.

best_available.why: Reaches both words through common phrases with a shared mood.

pairs.pair_note: LONELY carries the pair; DATE is serviceable backup.

hints.reason: Deep in my heart and the deep ocean are both plain usages of the same adjective.
The Titanic sank in the ocean and the film gave us My Heart Will Go On and the Heart of the Ocean necklace.
Heart pendants are the classic necklace; ocean only through the Titanic Heart of the Ocean necklace.

best_available.why: Broadest, needs no story knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: Two solid hints; NECKLACE leans on the film prop.

hints.reason: Me hearties is pirate talk, but the hint contains HEART as a substring, a rule failure.
Davy Jones is pirate lore; heart only via the Pirates of the Caribbean Davy Jones who cut out his own heart.
A pirate treasure chest and the heart in your chest; Dead Man's Chest ties both.

best_available.why: Clean double meaning understood by everyone.

pairs.pair_note: HEARTIES is a contains_target rule failure despite a good idea.

hints.reason: Diana was dubbed Queen of Hearts but was a princess, never queen; both sides lean on one nickname.
Hearts is a suit and the queen is a face card; the queen of hearts is one card.
The Queen of Hearts is the Wonderland villain, reaching both words through one famous story.

best_available.why: Most direct; the queen of hearts is a single physical object.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; DIANA is a fair but shakier nickname route.

hints.reason: The Claddagh is a ring with hands holding a heart, perfect if known but niche outside Irish circles.
Engagement ring is immediate; heart only through love and proposal.
Promise ring is a known term; heart via cross-my-heart sincerity, a loose route.

best_available.why: Ring is certain and heart-as-love is the most natural of the three loose heart routes.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; CLADDAGH is the best idea but too niche to carry the pair.

hints.reason: Hard rock and hard-hearted are both common compounds.
Heart of stone is idiomatic and stone is a plain synonym of rock.
Rock band is immediate; heart via Heart the rock band, a word-used-as-name route many players know.

best_available.why: Both compounds are everyday language.

pairs.pair_note: All three serve; BAND rewards music knowledge.

hints.reason: The heart is the symbol of love and the rose its flower.
Red heart and red rose are the default colours of both; a valid shared property.
Hearts and roses are the two Valentine icons.

best_available.why: One shared scene that contains both objects.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair across the board.

hints.reason: Blood pressure is a heart matter and salt is the thing doctors tell you raises it; one shared health scene.
Tears are salty; heart only through heartbreak making you cry.
Salt of the earth is idiomatic, but heart of the earth is not a phrase players reach for.

best_available.why: Blood pressure connects both through one familiar warning.

pairs.pair_note: PRESSURE is a good hint; EARTH is filler.

hints.reason: Long shadow is natural; a heart that longs is a different word sense and does not present itself.
Secrets of the heart and secrets kept in the shadows share a hidden mood but neither side is a set phrase.
Shadow of a doubt is idiomatic; heart has no doubt route.
Follow your heart, and a shadow follows you everywhere; a clean verb route.

best_available.why: Verb works literally for shadow and idiomatically for heart.

pairs.pair_note: FOLLOW is the only real hint; LONG and DOUBT are shadow-only.

hints.reason: Loan shark is immediate; heart has nothing to do with loans.
Cold-hearted is a set word; shark via cold-blooded or cold-eyed predator, a reasonable but looser property.

best_available.why: Shared cold-blooded property reaches both, if a little loosely for shark.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; COLD is close and could be argued up.

hints.reason: Snake charmer is immediate; heart via the heart charm on a bracelet and charming your way into a heart.
Heart and snake are two of the classic tattoo motifs, one shared scene.
Cold-hearted and cold-blooded snake are both familiar.

best_available.why: Both words are everyday tattoo imagery.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair; CHARM is the weakest PASS.

hints.reason: Charlotte is the spider in Charlotte's Web; there is no heart route from the name.
The heart pumps blood through veins and spider veins are a common term.

best_available.why: Anatomy plus a familiar compound.

pairs.pair_note: VEINS carries the pair alone.

hints.reason: Spring fever is a set phrase; heart only through a racing feverish heart or the love-fever song.
My heart leapt is idiomatic and to spring is to leap; a clean verb route.

best_available.why: Verb meaning covers spring directly and heart idiomatically.

pairs.pair_note: LEAP is good; FEVER is one-and-a-half sided.

hints.reason: The heart and star emoji are both among the most used.
Wish upon a star is immediate; heart via wishing with all your heart and the song's heart's-desire line.
Heart shape and star shape are two of the basic shapes children learn.

best_available.why: Both words are literally shape names.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; WISH is the softest.

hints.reason: Only works via the 1945 film Brief Encounter set at a railway station; neither word is reached from the hint itself.
Train tracks is immediate; heart has no tracks route.
Train wreck is a set phrase; heart via a wrecked heart as heartbreak, loose but readable.

best_available.why: Train is certain and heartbreak-as-wreck is a plausible jump.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; BRIEF is the weakest hint in the file.

hints.reason: Water flows; heart via blood flow, a secondary step.
Tears are water; heart only through heartbreak tears.
The heart is a pump and a water pump is an everyday object.

best_available.why: Direct function match for both.

pairs.pair_note: PUMP is excellent; the other two are soft.

hints.reason: Witches cast spells; heart via a love spell or being under someone's spell.
Snow White's witch-queen demands the girl's heart in a box; one famous story reaches both.
The Snow White huntsman is sent by the witch-queen to bring back a heart; both links depend on recalling that detail.

best_available.why: Snow White is the shared story everyone knows.

pairs.pair_note: SNOW is a story route on par with the POISON anchor.

hints.reason: Lone wolf is immediate; heart via lonely heart, a near-inflection but not the same word.
Huntsman kills the wolf in Red Riding Hood, but the heart link comes from a different story (Snow White); mixing two tales to reach the pair is a rescue.
Wild at heart is idiomatic and the wolf is the archetypal wild animal.

best_available.why: Shared property through a common idiom.

pairs.pair_note: WILD carries it; HUNTSMAN here is weaker than in HEART+WITCH.

hints.reason: Honey and sugar are twin sweeteners and pet names; sugar cubes are the classic horse treat.
Horses eat oats; honey oats is a familiar cereal and granola pairing.
Honeycomb, and grooming a horse with a comb.

best_available.why: Compound on one side, everyday grooming on the other.

pairs.pair_note: All three are good.

hints.reason: Ice cream is immediate; honey via creamed honey or honey and cream, not a set pairing.
Honey in tea and iced tea are both everyday.
Honey and lemon is a fixed pairing; ice via lemon ice or ice and a slice of lemon in a drink.

best_available.why: Both routes are drink-order plain.

pairs.pair_note: TEA is the clear serve; LEMON is a fair second.

hints.reason: Iron tonic is an old-fashioned supplement and honey tonics exist, but neither is a phrase players reach for.
Honey pot (Pooh) and cast-iron pot are both everyday.
Waffle iron is a compound and honey on waffles is a breakfast scene.

best_available.why: Compound plus a shared breakfast picture.

pairs.pair_note: Two good hints; TONIC is dated.

hints.reason: Honey sits beside jam as a spread and a key can jam in a lock; both routes are adjacent rather than direct.
Honey is sticky and sticky keys (keyboard or lock) are a familiar nuisance.
Honey bee is immediate; there is no bee route to key.

best_available.why: Shared property that is literally true of both.

pairs.pair_note: STICKY carries the pair; BEE is honey-only filler.

hints.reason: Mead is honey wine; king only via medieval mead halls and feasting kings.
Honey bee is immediate but hives have queens, not kings.
King Solomon is clear; honey only through a Song of Solomon line nobody would recall from the name.

best_available.why: Only hint touching both; honey is solid and the medieval court jump is reasonable.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; the pair has no obvious shared compound.

hints.reason: Honey is sweet; knights are not.
Honey wine on one side; knight only through the medieval feast setting.

best_available.why: The medieval setting is the only thread between the two words.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; a hard pair.

hints.reason: Candlelight is immediate; honey via beeswax or honey-scented candles, a step removed.
Honey is amber coloured and the amber light is a traffic signal; a valid shared property.

best_available.why: Colour route is direct on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: AMBER works; CANDLE is a beeswax stretch.

hints.reason: Honey badger is immediate; badger has no lion route.
Golden honey and the golden lion's mane; a shared colour property.
Samson killed a lion and later found honey in its carcass; the lion is known, the honey detail is for Bible readers.

best_available.why: Immediate colour association for both.

pairs.pair_note: GOLDEN serves; SAMSON is a true story route but niche.

hints.reason: A lunar month reaches moon; honey only via the honeymoon-is-a-month etymology, which the hint does not surface.
Wedding points straight at the compound honeymoon, which is the pair itself.
Harvest moon is a compound and beekeepers harvest honey.

best_available.why: Each side stands on its own without needing the pair compound.

pairs.pair_note: Two good hints; WEDDING is a pair-compound hint and should be confirmed acceptable in principle.

hints.reason: House mouse is immediate; honey has no house route beyond a beekeeping term.
Pooh and honey are inseparable, but there is no mouse in the Hundred Acre Wood.
Mouse trap and honey trap are both set phrases.

best_available.why: Two compounds with the same head word.

pairs.pair_note: TRAP alone; the other two are each one-sided.

hints.reason: Honey in tea is plain; night via a bedtime cup, a shared scene but not a phrase.
Honeymoon is a compound and the moon belongs to the night.

best_available.why: Compound plus a natural association.

pairs.pair_note: MOON carries it.

hints.reason: Ocean salt is immediate; salted honey is a niche flavour that the hint does not evoke.
Golden honey is plain; the ocean is only golden at a sunset, not a property players would name.

best_available.why: Honey is certain and a golden sea at sunset is at least a shared image, which is more than salted honey offers.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are one-sided and the pair needs a new idea.

hints.reason: Grog is pirate drink; the honey-in-grog recipe is too niche to count.
Pirates and rum are inseparable; honey via honey rum or a hot toddy, a secondary pairing.

best_available.why: Pirate is certain and honey rum is a real, if secondary, product.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; drink routes only half-reach honey.

hints.reason: Queen Bey is a famous nickname; honey only by chaining Bey to bee to honey.
Honey bee and queen bee are both compounds.
The hive makes honey and is ruled by a queen; one shared scene.

best_available.why: Two compounds sharing the same head word.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; BEYONCE is a two-step chain.

hints.reason: Contains HONEY as a substring, a rule failure regardless of the wedding link to ring.
Wedding ring is immediate; honey via the honeymoon that follows and honey as the spouse pet name.
Honey-glazed is a fixed compound; ring via the glazed ring doughnut.

best_available.why: Both halves are everyday; the honeymoon jump is natural.

pairs.pair_note: Two usable hints; HONEYMOON is a contains_target failure.

hints.reason: A drone is a male honey bee and a flying robot; clean double meaning.
Honey bee is immediate; robot only via the Transformers robot Bumblebee or robo-bee research.

best_available.why: One word with two genuine senses.

pairs.pair_note: DRONE is the pair's natural hint.

hints.reason: Honeycomb is immediate; there is no comb route to rock.
Rock candy is a compound; honey via honey candies and honey as a natural sweet.
Honey is amber coloured and amber is a fossil-resin gemstone, i.e. a rock.

best_available.why: Colour on one side and a literal stone on the other.

pairs.pair_note: Two usable hints; COMB is honey-only.

hints.reason: A drop of honey or honey drops, and drop shadow from design software.
To shadow someone is spy work and the honey trap is a spy tactic; one espionage scene.
Shadows stretch in the evening; honey does not stretch in any phrase players know.
Honeymoon is a compound and moonshadow or the moon casting shadows is natural.

best_available.why: Compound plus a plain physical association.

pairs.pair_note: Three usable hints; STRETCH is shadow-only.

hints.reason: Honey is sweet; sharks are not.
Honey badger is immediate; badger has no shark route.

best_available.why: Neither reaches shark; BADGER at least names a famous fearless predator that players loosely group with sharks, which is more than SWEET offers.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are honey-only and the pair needs a fresh idea (e.g. a predator or bait route).

hints.reason: Snake charmer is immediate; honey via honeyed, charming words, a figurative stretch.
Honey trap is a set phrase; snake trap is not something players would reach for.
A snake's forked tongue and a honeyed or honey-tongued speaker.

best_available.why: Literal for snake, idiomatic for honey.

pairs.pair_note: TONGUE carries it; CHARM is a fair second.

hints.reason: Honey trap is a set phrase and a spider's web is a trap.
Spiders catch flies, and you catch more flies with honey than vinegar.
Honey is sticky and so is a spider's web.

best_available.why: Literal shared property of both.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; all three serve.
